headline: AI Cloud growth offsets marketing drag, profit narrows
summary_short: Baidu's Q2 FY2026 revenue was RMB31.3 billion ($4.62 billion), down 4% y/y and 2% q/q, as AI Cloud Infra revenue grew 50% y/y to RMB7.3 billion while online marketing stayed under pressure; non-GAAP diluted EPS per ADS fell to RMB7.22 ($1.06) from RMB13.58 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue fell 4% y/y and 2% q/q to RMB31.3 billion ($4.62 billion) as online-marketing pressure offset AI Cloud demand. Baidu Core AI-powered Business revenue rose 25% y/y to RMB12.5 billion, now half of General Business revenue, led by AI Cloud Infra (+50% y/y, GPU Cloud +283% y/y). Non-GAAP operating margin narrowed to 12% (-2ppt y/y) as AI Cloud infrastructure costs outpaced revenue. Net margin fell to 7% (-15ppt y/y) on lower investment fair-value gains, a wider FX loss, and higher tax. Operating cash flow was positive for a fourth straight quarter at RMB3.4 billion; total cash and investments were RMB283.1 billion. No numeric forward guidance was given; the release disclosed progress on Baidu's Hong Kong dual-primary listing conversion.
confidence_notes: KPI values sourced directly from the primary EX-99.1 press release (SEC 6-K), not from the resolver's shard kpis object -- the shard's eps_usd entry (value 7.22, unit 'USD') conflates the release's actual RMB7.22 non-GAAP diluted EPS per ADS figure with a USD unit tag; the correct USD equivalent per the release is $1.06. RMB-to-USD translations throughout use the release's own H.10 rate of RMB6.7851/$1 as of June 30, 2026. The release presents two non-additive revenue classification schemes (Core/Legacy/Others AI-powered-business split vs. Online-Marketing/Others split); this summary follows the AI-powered-business framing the release leads with. All revenue and operational data are unaudited per company disclosure.

drivers.explanation: CEO stated the online marketing business remains under pressure, while emphasizing growth in AI Cloud, AI Applications and Apollo Go reflects Baidu's transition to an AI-first company.
CFO attributed AI-powered Business reaching half of General Business revenue to sustained AI Cloud Infra momentum and the AI Applications portfolio's continued growth in capabilities and use cases.
Company attributes growth to mounting demand for public cloud-based AI computing; GPU Cloud revenue grew 283% y/y, accelerating from 184% growth the prior quarter.
Not directly attributed by the release; derived from disclosed cost moves -- cost of revenue rose 4% y/y on AI Cloud business costs while total revenue fell 4% y/y, compressing margin.
Company attributes the net income decline partly to a decrease in fair value gain from long-term investments and a larger net foreign-exchange loss, plus higher income tax expense.
